narrative:
Short impact summary

Second Assessment of Climate Change for the Baltic Sea Basin (2015), published by Springer Nature, has been cited 385 times — enough that OpenAlex puts it in the top 1% of works in its field and year. Beyond that, it has been downloaded 755 times.

Full narrative

Second Assessment of Climate Change for the Baltic Sea Basin by The BACC II Author Team was published by Springer Nature in 2015. It is part of the Regional climate studies series. Conceptually, the work connects to Baltic sea, Structural basin, Climate change, Geography and Oceanography.

OpenAlex records 385 citations. That places it in the top 1% of works in its field and year of publication. Citations peaked in 2021 with 77 citing works. Notable citing venues include Water, The Science of The Total Environment and Earth System Dynamics. Of 62 citation statements scite has classified, 2 support its claims, 60 mention it in passing, and none contradict it. The citing works include 272 journal articles, 26 book chapters and 23 preprints. They come from 40 countries, led by Germany, Sweden and Finland.

It has been downloaded 755 times via OAPEN. Open Library reports a combined count of 2 reading logs and catalog editions. Its subject matter aligns with Climate action among the Sustainable Development Goals.
